ev.q: Using COVID-19 patient electronic health record data from 41 U.S. health care systems
the overall use of mAb was infrequent, with mean monthly use at 4% or less
SARS-CoV-2 positive patients of Hispanic ethnicity received mAb 57.7% less often
Mean monthly remdesivir use among inpatients who were White, Black, Asian, or Other race was 29.0%
Patients who were Black, Asian, or Other race received mAb 22.4%, 48.3%, and 46.5%, respectively, less often than did White patients
this study assessed receipt of medications for COVID-19 treatment by race

methods_quotes.q: pairwise Wilcoxon signed rank tests, with p-values indicated as p w , were used to assess whether treatment receipt differed systematically over time
The grand means (means of relative monthly treatment disparities) were calculated, and t-tests for statistical difference from zero
relative monthly treatment disparities were calculated as the difference in percentage of patients treated
Results were considered statistically significant for p-values <0.05.
the aggregate data structure did not allow for adjustment of demographic or clinical factors that might be correlated with race and ethnicity
